model: P&C insurer free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; pre-tax operating income after tax and regulatory capital retention, net debt held at zero, preferred and other equity deducted in the bridge)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred shares and other equity (LRCNs) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 annual; kpis PreferredEquity FY2025 1,766. The flows are NOI attributable to all shareholders (before the ~$90m of preferred/other-equity distributions: NOI to shareholders 3,518 vs to common 3,428, Table 28.5), so the claim is deducted here once at book rather than in the flows.

historical_growth.basis_note: IFRS 17 period only (FY2022-FY2025) for the 3-year figures. 5-year figures span the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 break AND the June 2021 RSA acquisition (equity raise, revenue step-up) and are reported for completeness, not as a trend.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 insurance revenue growth: operating DPW 3-year CAGR 6.1% (FY2022 21,005 -> FY2025 25,067; +4% constant currency in FY2025) blended with the FY2025 Section 13 industry outlook (personal lines high-single to low-double digit, commercial/specialty low-to-mid single digit), haircut because insurance revenue lags written premium and UK&I personal-lines exits held statutory insurance revenue to 1.3% CAGR.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year equity CAGR 9.6% diverges >30% from 3-year revenue CAGR 2.3%: equity compounds from retained earnings (payout ~40% of NOI) while IFRS 17 insurance revenue was held flat by the UK&I personal-lines and Codan Denmark exits. Growth is therefore judged on operating DPW (6.1%), not on statutory revenue. The 5-year figures (revenue 19.0%, EPS 20.6%, equity 16.8%) are RSA-acquisition and accounting-regime artefacts.
historical_growth.notes: No owner-FCF CAGR: free cash flow is not a meaningful series for an insurer (operating cash flow is premium/claims timing plus investment-portfolio flows), and the FCFE basis used here is only definable on IFRS 17 data. NOIPS grew 17.2% a year from a CAT-heavy FY2022 base (11.92 -> 19.21); the company's stated objective is 10% NOIPS growth over time and ROE outperformance of the industry by 500 bp (670 bp achieved over 10 years).

scenario_narratives.base: Intact earns a mid-cycle ~90% combined ratio on insurance revenue that grows 5% in 2026 and fades to 2.5% by 2035, with operating investment income above $1.6bn growing with the float and distribution income (BrokerLink, On Side) compounding at ~10%. Pre-tax operating margin normalises from FY2025's low-CAT 16.6% to ~15% and holds there; ~70 cents of equity is retained per dollar of revenue growth and the rest is free cash flow to equity, discounted at an 8.5% CAD cost of equity. The FY2025 NOIPS of $19.21 does not repeat in 2026 on this basis (~$18 after normal CATs), which is the main reason the base value sits near the current price rather than above it.
scenario_narratives.bull: The hard market in Canadian personal lines runs through 2027, commercial repositioning finishes without further shrinkage, the UK&I doubling and US specialty ambitions deliver 6-7% organic growth for three years, and the combined ratio holds ~88.5% on better pricing and claims-supply-chain economics. NOIPS compounds at the company's 10% objective, the cost of equity is 8.0% and terminal FCFE is capped at 17x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Commercial and specialty pricing softens from 2026, personal auto growth is capped by provincial rate regulation, CAT losses run above the $1.2bn guidance as severity trends worsen, and UK&I stays a mid-90s combined-ratio business. Margin settles ~13% pre-tax, growth ~2%, cost of equity 9.5% and terminal FCFE capped at 12x -- a 2024-style year (combined ratio 92.2%, NOIPS $14.43) becomes the run-rate rather than the trough.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A P&C insurer is valued on the earnings stream its underwriting and float produce after the capital it must retain to keep writing, not on reported free cash flow. Pre-tax operating income (underwriting + operating net investment income + distribution income - finance costs - other operating) is taxed at the operating rate, less equity retained in proportion to growth, and the remainder is capitalised at a CAD cost of equity with net debt at zero and preferred equity deducted once in the bridge. The anchor is the IFRS 17 period only; FY2025 is treated as a cyclically strong year (CATs 2 points under plan) and normalised to a ~90% combined ratio. Cross-checked against BVPS x sustainable P/B, which at a 16% mid-cycle ROE reproduces the current price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Stale anchors: balance sheet, share count, capital margin and preferred equity are at 31 Dec 2025; Q1/Q2-2026 interims were not in the folder. Price near the 52-week low suggests 2026 evidence the model has not seen.
Catastrophe losses: the $1.2bn annual guidance was undershot by ~$460m in FY2025; a 2024-style year (Q3-2024 combined ratio 103.9%) takes ~$2.5 off NOIPS.
Pricing cycle: Canadian personal lines are in a hard market; commercial/specialty is already softening. Each combined-ratio point is ~$230m pre-tax (~$1.0/share).
Investment income: 2026 guidance >$1.6bn rests on a 3.9% book yield; reinvestment at 3.7% means NII grows only with assets.
UK&I and US specialty execution: UK&I combined ratio 94.8% FY2025 vs Canada 86.8%; the doubling ambition carries integration risk (DLG commercial book).
Capital deployment: the 3.7bn capital margin is treated as distributable; a large acquisition at a high multiple would convert it into goodwill.
Operating tax rate was flattered to 21.4% by UK&I recoveries; the model's 22% could prove low.
Equity-model mechanics: the terminal multiple cap (15x base) binds below Gordon; a re-rating to the 10-year upper range (18x) adds ~10% to the base value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of); 52-week range 236.92-305.52; CAD quote on the TSX, same currency as the filings so no FX bridge.
data_sources.financials: research/IFC.TO/Reports/IFC.TO_Metrics.csv (core_metrics via export_csv.py) and kpis table; FY2025 operating build from IFC.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt Table 2.1 (lines 2185-2213: underwriting income 2,717, operating NII 1,632, distribution income 546, finance costs -239, other operating -181, PTOI 4,475, NOI to common 3,428, operating ETR 21.4%, BVPS 107.35, OROE 19.5%, total capital margin 3,722, adjusted debt-to-capital 16.5%), Table 28.5 (NOI to shareholders 3,518), share count line 6778, NCIB and subsequent events lines 4558-4568, Section 13 industry outlook lines 3409-3419, CAT guidance line 2971, investment income guidance line 3049.
data_sources.qualitative: IFC.TO_Analysis.json was not yet written when this valuation was built (the qualitative analyst was running concurrently); the industry and strategy framing come from the FY2025 MD&A and info.json's business summary. Re-read the Analysis JSON on the next refresh and revisit the scenario weights.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: IFRS 17 insurance revenue, FY2025 (IFC.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt; kpis InsuranceRevenue). Operating DPW FY2025 was 25,067 (+4% constant currency); operating net underwriting revenue (the combined-ratio denominator) is ~23,000, derived as underwriting income 2,717 / (1 - 0.882). Insurance revenue is used as the engine's top line because it is the statutory IFRS 17 line; growth is judged from DPW and the industry outlook because insurance revenue lags written premium by roughly a year.
inputs.share_count_basis: 177,631,629 common shares outstanding at 31 December 2025 (FY2025 annual, line 6778) plus ~0.2m option dilution (diluted weighted average 178.3m vs basic 178.1m, Table 28.11). Held FLAT: NCIB repurchases (732,339 shares / $198m in FY2025; 70,072 shares post year-end to 10 Feb 2026; renewed for up to 3% from 17 Feb 2026) are a use of the FCFE already counted in the flows, and share-based plans are settled with market-purchased shares (SharesPurchasedForSBPPlans $196m FY2025), so SBC creates no issuance.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO. The flow is free cash flow to equity: total finance costs ($239m FY2025 on $4,426m of debt plus hybrids) are already inside pre-tax operating income, so deducting debt again would double-count it. total_debt and cash are recorded for reference only. Adjusted debt-to-total capital 16.5% at 31 Dec 2025 vs ~20% internal target; total leverage ratio 24.5%.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCFE on the model basis: pre-tax operating income 4,475 less operating tax at 21.4% (958) = 3,517, less capital retention to support ~4% DPW growth at the FY2025 common-equity-to-insurance-revenue ratio (0.71 x 4% x 26,950 = ~755) = ~2,762. For reference, FY2025 cash returned to common holders was 1,037 dividends + 198 NCIB + 196 share-plan purchases = 1,431, and total capital margin rose 832 to 3,722 -- the business generated more distributable capital than it distributed.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow (operating cash flow 4,388 less purchases of intangibles and P&E 457). Not a valuation input for an insurer: operating cash flow is dominated by premium/claims timing and investment-portfolio flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual, Note on share-based payments: equity-settled share-based payment plans' expense 147 (FY2024 104); Metrics.csv StockBasedComp 147. Settled with shares purchased in the market, so it is a cash cost with no dilution.
inputs.interest_income_note: Operating net investment income (1,632 FY2025; 2026 guidance 'more than $1.6 billion') is core earnings for a P&C insurer -- the float is policyholder-funded and is NOT excess cash. Retained inside the margin, not stripped out.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, regularMarketTime); 52-week range 236.92-305.52, so the price sits within 2% of its 52-week low
inputs.balance_sheet_note: STALE ANCHOR FLAG: the latest filing in the folder is the FY2025 annual report (31 Dec 2025 balance sheet). Q1-2026 (May 2026) and Q2-2026 (Aug 2026) interims were not in Extracted/ at build time, so net debt, preferred equity, capital margin and the share count are nine months old and FY2026 is judged from FY2025 guidance alone. Refresh these from the Q2-2026 or Q3-2026 MD&A before relying on the entry price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, CAD-denominated flows: Government of Canada 10-year ~3.4% (Oct 2026) + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta ~0.8 (P&C insurer, low-beta) = ~7.4% market-implied; lifted to 8.5% base for catastrophe-loss volatility, UK&I/US specialty execution and the model's reliance on a mid-cycle combined ratio. Bull 8.0%, bear 9.5%. Same family as IAG.AX (9.0%, AUD) and GL (9.0%, USD) in this folder, set lower here for a 19.5% operating ROE, AA-rated-subsidiary franchise with a 10-year average ROE outperformance of 670 bp. This is an equity rate, not a WACC: no debt term because the flow is after finance costs.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 lease expense (depreciation and interest) is already inside pre-tax operating income; lease liabilities (~$674m discounted at 31 Dec 2025) are not added to net debt because the flow is post-lease. Charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests were nil at 31 Dec 2025 (13 at FY2024, bought out); NOI attributable to NCI was 0 in FY2025 (Table 28.5). No adjustment.
inputs.tax_note: Operating effective tax rate 21.4% FY2025 (20.2% FY2024, 26.2% FY2023), FY2025 flattered by UK&I tax recoveries. Base path 22% flat, bull 21.5%, bear 23%.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = IFRS 17 insurance revenue. ebitda_margin_path = (pre-tax operating income + SBC expense) / insurance revenue, where PTOI = underwriting income + operating net investment income + distribution income - total finance costs - other operating expense (Table 2.1). sbc_pct_path = equity-settled SBC expense / revenue (deducted on the house basis; the street basis adds it back). da_pct_path = 0 (D&A is inside PTOI; acquisition-related intangible amortisation of 575 is non-operating and excluded on both bases). capex_pct_path = equity retained to hold the common-equity-to-insurance-revenue ratio (~0.71x at FY2025) through the growth path, i.e. ~0.7 x revenue growth. cash_tax_rate_path = operating effective tax rate. wc_capture_pct = 0. wacc = cost of equity. Net debt 0; preferred shares and other equity deducted in equity_bridge at carrying value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes an insurer to 'BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. Overridden to FCFE at cost of equity on the engine route, the precedent set by IAG.AX, GL, PRU and LGEN.L in this folder, for three reasons: (1) IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 breaks the book-value series at FY2021/FY2022 (total assets 66.3bn -> 53.7bn, BVPS 89.28 -> 82.69 restated), leaving only four clean compounding years; (2) Intact distributes roughly 40% of NOI (dividends 1,037 + NCIB 198 + plan purchases 196 = 1,431 on NOI to common 3,428) and holds a 3.7bn total capital margin for M&A, so the value sits in the distributable earnings stream rather than in a book-compounding rate; (3) the engine route validates by construction and produces the workbook. BVPS x EXIT P/B CROSS-CHECK (memo): BVPS 107.35 at 31 Dec 2025; sustainable P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g): at a 16% mid-cycle operating ROE (10-year outperformance of the industry benchmark by 670 bp), g 2.5%, CoE 8.5% -> 2.25x -> ~$241; at the FY2025 19.5% OROE -> 2.83x -> ~$304. The current price (~2.26x book) prices the mid-cycle ROE, not the FY2025 peak. ACCOUNTING REGIME: FY2013-FY2021 are IFRS 4 and are not comparable to FY2022+ (IFRS 17 restated); every anchor, margin and CAGR in this file comes from FY2022-FY2025 unless stated. FY2025 was a low-CAT year (combined ratio 88.2%, CATs ~2 points below the $1.2bn annual guidance); the four-year IFRS 17 average combined ratio is ~89.8% and the base case normalises to ~90% in FY2026. ANALYSIS JSON: IFC.TO_Analysis.json had not been written by the qualitative analyst when this build ran; narratives rest on the FY2025 MD&A (Section 13 industry outlook, Section 23 capital management) and the industry context in info.json. The 2026 interims are also absent (see balance_sheet_note).

bear.growth_rationale: Commercial and specialty lines soften from 2026, Canadian personal auto returns to regulated rate caps (Alberta-style), UK&I shrinks further after the personal-lines exit; growth ~2% is claims-inflation pass-through only.
bear.margin_rationale: Combined ratio ~92% (FY2024 level; CAT losses trend above the $1.2bn guidance as weather severity rises; UK&I combined ratio stays mid-90s), NII flat as reinvestment yields fall below book yield, distribution income growth slows to 5%. PTOI margin ~12.5% after SBC.
bear.capex_rationale: Lower growth needs less retained capital, but held above 0.7 x growth because a weaker underwriting result pushes the group to rebuild capital margin and reserve margins rather than distribute.

base.growth_rationale: Insurance revenue. FY2026 5.0%: operating DPW grew 4% in FY2025 with personal lines strong and commercial lines deliberately repositioned; the FY2025 industry outlook calls for high-single-digit personal lines and low-to-mid single-digit commercial growth, and BrokerLink/On Side distribution income is guided to 10%+ a year. Fades from rate-driven mid-single digits to 2.5% terminal as the hard market in Canadian personal lines normalises. No acquisition contribution: the 3.7bn capital margin is treated as FCFE, not as pre-funded M&A.
base.margin_rationale: (PTOI + SBC) / insurance revenue. FY2025 actual 17.2% (PTOI 4,475 + SBC 147 on 26,950) in a low-CAT year (combined ratio 88.2%). FY2026 base 15.5%: combined ratio normalised to ~90% (four-year IFRS 17 average ~89.8%, FY2026 CAT guidance $1.2bn) on ~24.2bn of net underwriting revenue = ~2,420 underwriting income, + operating NII ~1,650 (guidance >1.6bn, book yield 3.9% vs 3.7% reinvestment), + distribution income ~600 (10% growth), - finance costs ~245, - other operating ~190 = PTOI ~4,235 (+156 SBC) on ~28,300 revenue. Drifts to 15.1% as commercial/specialty pricing softens, partly offset by distribution income compounding at 10% and NII growing with the float.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold common equity at ~0.71x insurance revenue (19,070 / 26,950 at 31 Dec 2025) through the growth path: ~0.7 x revenue growth. Terminal 1.8% = 0.7 x 2.5% terminal growth, so the terminal flow is self-consistent with the Gordon growth rate. No separate capital rebuild: total capital margin of 3.7bn and MCT 195% are already above target.
base.terminal_cap_rationale: Terminal FCFE capped at 15x, roughly the 10-year median P/E on NOIPS for Intact (13-18x range; 12.6x at the current price on FY2025 NOIPS). Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would imply 16.7x, so the cap binds slightly.

bull.growth_rationale: Hard market persists through 2027 in Canadian personal lines (high-single to low-double digit industry growth), UK&I doubling ambition and US specialty reach ~$10bn DPW by 2030 organically, distribution income compounds at 12%+.
bull.margin_rationale: Combined ratio holds ~88.5% (FY2025 88.2%; underlying loss ratio improving on pricing sophistication and claims supply-chain investment), NII grows with assets at a 3.9% book yield, distribution income 12%. Still below the FY2025 17.2% peak because FY2025 CATs were ~2 points below plan.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bull is trimmed because the FY2025 result was a low-CAT year that already sits at the top of the historical margin range, and the stock's slide to within 2% of its 52-week low (from 305) suggests the market has seen 2026 evidence -- interim results, CAT activity or pricing -- that is not in this folder. Bear is lifted for the same missing-interims reason: the FY2026 year is judged from FY2025 guidance only. Rebalance toward 15/50/35 once the Q2/Q3-2026 MD&A is extracted and the combined ratio trend is known.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
